# Restoring golden to another cluster

Generated by SetDrift test from a snapshot of `golden` (Kubernetes v1.35.0), taken 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC.

Follow the steps in order. Commands run from this directory. SetDrift ran
none of them; the ones marked *source cluster* are the only ones that change
it. Set these first:

```sh
SRC='<source-context>'   # kubeconfig context of golden
DST=<target-context>   # kubeconfig context of the new cluster
```


## 1. Check the target cluster

```sh
kubectl --context "$DST" version
kubectl --context "$DST" get nodes
```

The source runs Kubernetes v1.35.0. Use the same minor version or a newer one;
`kubectl apply` reports resources whose API a newer version removed.

## 2. Apply the export

Everything that can be applied: CRDs, cluster-scoped objects, then each namespace.

```sh
kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side -k .
```


## 3. Secrets

These files hold `SETDRIFT_REDACTED` instead of secret values and were not applied with
the rest; Pods that use them wait until they exist. Supply the values one
of these ways. In a Secret marked *merge*, a controller writes the other
keys: only the keys listed are restored, and the controller's are left to
it.

**A. Copy them from the source cluster**, while it still exists. The values
go straight from one cluster to the other and are never written to disk:

```sh
kubectl --context "$SRC" -n shop get configmap app-config -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.uid, .metadata.resourceVersion, .metadata.creationTimestamp, .metadata.managedFields, .metadata.ownerReferences, .metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"], .status)' | kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f -
kubectl --context "$SRC" -n argocd get secret repo-platform -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.uid, .metadata.resourceVersion, .metadata.creationTimestamp, .metadata.managedFields, .metadata.ownerReferences, .metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"], .status)' | kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f -
kubectl --context "$SRC" -n shop get secret db-creds -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.uid, .metadata.resourceVersion, .metadata.creationTimestamp, .metadata.managedFields, .metadata.ownerReferences, .metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"], .status)' | kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f -
kubectl --context "$SRC" -n shop get secret ecr-pull -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.uid, .metadata.resourceVersion, .metadata.creationTimestamp, .metadata.managedFields, .metadata.ownerReferences, .metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"], .status)' | kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f -
kubectl --context "$SRC" -n shop get deployment.apps api -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.uid, .metadata.resourceVersion, .metadata.creationTimestamp, .metadata.managedFields, .metadata.ownerReferences, .metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"], .status)' | kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f -
```

**B. Fill in the files** from wherever the values are kept, then apply each
file. Values under `data:` are base64 (`printf %s 'value' | base64`). Keys
a controller writes are not in the files.

- `redacted/namespaces/shop/configmap/app-config.yaml.redacted` (ConfigMap shop/app-config)
  - line 3: `data.application.properties`
- `redacted/namespaces/argocd/secret/repo-platform.yaml.redacted` (Secret argocd/repo-platform)
  - line 11: `stringData.password`
  - line 12: `stringData.url`
- `redacted/namespaces/shop/secret/db-creds.yaml.redacted` (Secret shop/db-creds)
  - line 3: `data.password`
  - line 4: `data.username`
- `redacted/namespaces/shop/secret/ecr-pull.yaml.redacted` (Secret shop/ecr-pull)
  - line 3: `data..dockerconfigjson`
- `redacted/namespaces/shop/deployment.apps/api.yaml.redacted` (Deployment shop/api)
  - line 18: `spec.template.spec.containers[api].env[DB_PASSWORD].value`

```sh
kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f redacted/namespaces/shop/configmap/app-config.yaml.redacted
kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f redacted/namespaces/argocd/secret/repo-platform.yaml.redacted
kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f redacted/namespaces/shop/secret/db-creds.yaml.redacted
kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f redacted/namespaces/shop/secret/ecr-pull.yaml.redacted
kubectl --context "$DST" apply --server-side --field-manager=setdrift-restore -f redacted/namespaces/shop/deployment.apps/api.yaml.redacted
```

**C. External Secrets Operator.** external-secrets/ has an ExternalSecret
for each Secret (see its README); those marked *merge* add their keys to
the Secret the controller creates (`creationPolicy: Merge`). Put the values
in your secret manager, install the operator and its store, then apply the
directory. On AWS, `setdrift secrets export` copies the values from the
source cluster into Secrets Manager or Parameter Store (it shows a plan
first and never writes or prints a value); elsewhere, create the remote
secrets the README lists, with their keys:

```sh
kubectl --context "$DST" apply -k external-secrets/
```

Workloads read these values when they start. Restart the workloads in
these namespaces so every component uses the restored values:

```sh
kubectl --context "$DST" -n argocd rollout restart deployment,statefulset,daemonset
kubectl --context "$DST" -n shop rollout restart deployment,statefulset,daemonset
```

**Amazon ECR tokens expire.** shop/ecr-pull holds an ECR token (`111122223333.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`)
that lasts 12 hours: a copied, filled-in or stored value stops working
within a day. Restore what refreshes it in the source cluster (often a
CronJob, or a controller that rewrites the Secret), or drop the Secret and
let nodes pull with their IAM role: on EKS, a node role with ECR read access
(AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly) pulls from its own account, and from
other accounts whose repository policy allows it.

2 objects other than Secrets hold secret values (see the files above). Moving
those values into Secrets and referencing them makes the next export apply
without this step.

Service account tokens (shop/ci-token) are created again with new values, and
tokens copied out of the source cluster stop working in the new one.

## 4. Check the result

`setdrift verify` dry-runs the export against the new cluster and reports
what differs; nothing should be left except explained differences.

```sh
setdrift verify --context "$DST" .
kubectl --context "$DST" get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase!=Running,status.phase!=Succeeded
```
